decision.label: REAL-MIXTURE ADAPTATION IS VIABLE BUT NO CLEAR PRODUCT GAIN
decision.blinded_comparison: S1R clearly preferred 0/6 groups vs zero-shot (bar >=3/6); explicit ties in c2/c3, inconclusive c7, tie c8, faint c6 edge for S1R, ambiguous c1; no deletion, no passthrough, no instability heard; c3 selectivity pattern audibly preserved
decision.protocol_caveats: headphone session (S1W was speakers) -> no cross-stage timbre claims; one pass only; substantial owner fatigue recorded

checkpoint.selected: full_upd01500 (DEV-only; all section-32 validity checks true at every eval)

machine_side.test_generalization: 28 S1W-identical windows, 14 unseen recordings: zero collapse, click retention -0.96 dB vs zero-shot -1.20 dB, no passthrough drift
machine_side.sealed_primary: 6 groups: S1R within +-0.2 dB RMS of zero-shot, transient retention slightly better on all six, zero collapse
machine_side.interpretation: stable real-domain adaptation without catastrophic forgetting; no large machine-side separation win - confirmed by human listening (verdict B)
